\begin{document}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
    Rossman defined the notion of criticality inspired by Switching lemmas and showed that bounds on criticality imply  average case lower bounds, PRGs, Fourier tail bounds, Learning algorithms and satisfiability algorithms.   
    We study the criticality of \demorgan formulae and show that a \demorgan formula with $L$ leaves has criticality $O(\sqrt{L})$. Our approach involves a canonical decision tree construction, Karchmer-Wigderson games, Shrinkage, a new structural lemma for the Formulae under random restrictions which we call as the Banyan decomposition lemma, and an analysis using probabilistic methods combined with convexity arguments.   
\end{abstract}
